title: No Verified Incident Can Justify Dog-Trade Safety Claims
excerpt: No police seizure, court verdict, or health alert is documented here. Public safety needs records, quarantine, and a clear abolition path by 2030.
body_html:
A rabies exposure can turn fatal after symptoms begin. No courtroom verdict, police seizure, intercepted shipment, or named Vietnamese health alert is documented here to support claims about a specific dog-trade incident. That gap matters. Public anger must rest on records, not invented scenes or sweeping claims.

Safety claims need proof

“Farm-raised” cannot function as a safety certificate. Any lawful supply chain would need traceability, veterinary oversight, transport controls, and quarantine compliance. A claim alone proves none of these. Authorities and operators should publish licenses, inspection records, origin documents, and test results.

Rabies leaves no room for delay

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, then seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance supports immediate care.

Records before permission

Vietnamese families deserve protection from stolen pets, illicit transport, unsafe handling, and enforcement gaps. Separate household exposure risks and commercial supply-chain risks both demand honest oversight; neither permits fabricated proof.

Sign SDE’s national petition calling for complete abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition and add your name to a public demand for accountable reform.
